```plato
//==
// # Primitives
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Primitive interface obligations
//  - The derived array surface
//  - The derived Integer surface
//  - The derived Number surface

library Primitives
{
    //==
    // # Primitive interface obligations
    //
    // The handful of members the `primitive` declarations in `primitives.plato` owe
    // their interface lists but that the host contract does NOT supply. Everything a
    // backend must implement natively is in `intrinsics.library.plato`; what is left
    // is derivable in Plato from those intrinsics, so it belongs here rather than
    // growing the porting checklist:
    //
    //   * the two identity conversions (`Number.ToNumber`, `Integer.ToInteger`),
    //     which exist so a body generic over `IReal` or `IWhole` can name the carrier;
    //   * `Number.Inverse` and the two `Lerp`s, one-line formulas over arithmetic
    //     the host already provides;
    //   * `Boolean.LessThanOrEquals`, read off the `Compare` intrinsic (false orders
    //     before true).
    //
    // Without these the generated members throw, so every derived body that reaches
    // them — and `IReal`/`IWhole`-generic code reaches ToNumber/ToInteger constantly —
    // throws with it.

    //==
    // # Number

    // The number itself: `IReal.ToNumber` on the carrier type is the identity.
    // It exists so a body generic over IReal can drop to a plain Number.
    ToNumber(self: Number): Number
        => self;
```
